title: Earnest Money and Deposits Due on the Home Purchase Agreement
content:
Under the Home Purchase Agreement the buyer posts initial earnest money and, where they apply, extra deposit components at signing, and later an additional deposit after construction starts. Collection percentages, minimums, caps and day counts below are those of the agreement's collection.

## 1. Initial earnest money

The initial earnest money is the greater of (a) the collection's initial earnest money percentage of the contract price, rounded half up to the cent, and (b) the collection's minimum initial earnest money. The contract price is the base price plus the lot premium.

**VA cap.** Where the buyer's rate lock with Calloway Home Mortgage on this agreement carries the VA loan program, the initial earnest money is capped at the collection's VA initial earnest money cap. The VA cap applies to the initial earnest money only and never to the extra components below.

**Reservation funds.** A transferred reservation deposit counts toward the initial earnest money.

## 2. Extra components due at signing

On top of the initial earnest money, the buyer posts at signing:

- the collection's outside-lender or cash extra deposit percentage of the contract price, rounded half up to the cent, when the buyer finances with an outside lender or pays cash;
- the collection's extra earnest money for a home-sale contingency, when the agreement carries a home-sale contingency;
- the lot premium deposit required by the Homesite Reservation conversion terms, when the homesite was reserved first, reduced by the premium holding fee and the creditable extension fees moved from the reservation.

## 3. Additional deposit

The clause of these terms stating that an additional deposit of the collection's additional deposit percentage of the contract price is due after construction starts is **no longer in force**; the amount of the additional deposit due is set by the current basis that superseded it.

The deadline remains in force: **the additional deposit must post within the collection's additional deposit days (calendar days) after the construction start date.** Counting starts the day after the construction start date and the last counted day is included. The construction start date is the date on the agreement record on which the foundation was started. A missed additional deposit is a buyer default, handled under the agreement's buyer default and termination terms.

| Posting day of the additional deposit, counted from the day after the construction start date | Within the deadline? |
|---|---|
| Any day up to and including the last counted day | Yes, on time |
| The day after the last counted day or later | No, missed |

*Boundary illustration (hypothetical).* With a 10-day deadline and a construction start date of 4 May, counting runs 5 May through 14 May. A deposit posting on 14 May is on time; one posting on 15 May is late.

## 4. How deposits are paid

Any single deposit payment above the collection's wire threshold must be a wire. A card payment may not exceed the collection's card cap, and a cap of zero means card is not accepted.

## 5. Worked figures (hypothetical agreement)

A hypothetical agreement with a contract price of 480000.00 in a collection whose figures are 2.0 percent, a minimum of 7500.00, an outside-lender or cash percentage of 2.0 and a VA cap of 5000.00:

- Initial earnest money: 2.0 percent of 480000.00 is 9600.00, which is greater than 7500.00, so 9600.00.
- If the buyer's Calloway Home Mortgage rate lock on this agreement is on the VA program, the initial earnest money is capped at 5000.00.
- If the buyer pays cash, 2.0 percent of 480000.00, 9600.00, is due at signing in addition, and no VA cap applies to that component.

superseded_clauses: An additional deposit of additional_deposit_pct percent of the contract price is due after construction starts.
